newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower on Friday with many players taking their profits ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.17 points, 0.31 percent, to close at 696.50 points after touching a high of 700.23. The index was off 7.98 points, or 1.13 percent, on the week.
In the broader market, however, gainers led losers by 64 to 55 on Friday, with 66 counters unchanged. Turnover was 410.9 billion rupiah on a volume of 192 million shares.
Brokers said the market was likely to mixed on Monday with the index moving around the 695-700 level in the coming week.
Corporate action news such as a stock split, bonus share issues and expansion plans could boost market sentiment towards certain medium and small-sized companies, brokers said.
"Indications of 1996 earnings of some companies will also boost buying interest in some counters," a local broker said.
Brokers said overall market sentiment on Friday was relatively weak with buying interest only in certain medium and small-sized issues, with many foreign buyers on the sidelines.
Brokers said the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the market.
Property firm Elang Realty and shoe-maker Ganda Wangsa were among the active secondaries.
Elang Realty was the most active stock on locally-led profit taking, off 50 rupiah to 825 rupiah on 17.1 million shares after touching a high of 950 rupiah.
Brokers said it was actively traded on market talk that it had been targeted by businesman Johannes Kotjo for a takeover. Elang Realty refused to comment, and Kotjo was not available.

Ganda Wangsa rose 225 rupiah to 1,125 rupiah on a volume of 5.8 million shares, amid market speculation on the agenda for a shareholders' meeting due on March 24. Brokers said there was speculation of a stock split or bonus share issue, but company officials were unavailable for comment.
Cocoa processing company Cahaya Kalbar was actively traded, rising 175 rupiah to 2,550 rupiah on a volume of 1.6 million shares on fresh buying on better-than-expected 1996 results.
"Its 1996 net exceeded many analysts' target," a broker with foreign firm said.
Blue chips car maker Astra International was also active following a report that company executives were in Japan to discuss Indonesia's national car policy.
"The visit has sparked speculation that Astra might be involved in the national car project," one broker said.
